name: Frets On Fire
description: Miyako came to the flea kingdom with a ukulele. She became good friends with local flea residents and played beautiful music for them every day. In return, the fleas made a bigger ukulele for her: it has $$$n$$$ strings , and each string has $$$(10^{18} + 1)$$$ frets numerated from $$$0$$$ to $$$10^{18}$$$. The fleas use the array $$$s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n$$$ to describe the ukulele's tuning, that is, the pitch of the $$$j$$$-th fret on the $$$i$$$-th string is the integer $$$s_i + j$$$. Miyako is about to leave the kingdom, but the fleas hope that Miyako will answer some last questions for them. Each question is in the form of: "How many different pitches are there, if we consider frets between $$$l$$$ and $$$r$$$ (inclusive) on all strings?" Miyako is about to visit the cricket kingdom and has no time to answer all the questions. Please help her with this task! Formally, you are given a matrix with $$$n$$$ rows and $$$(10^{18}+1)$$$ columns, where the cell in the $$$i$$$-th row and $$$j$$$-th column ($$$0 \le j \le 10^{18}$$$) contains the integer $$$s_i + j$$$. You are to answer $$$q$$$ queries, in the $$$k$$$-th query you have to answer the number of distinct integers in the matrix from the $$$l_k$$$-th to the $$$r_k$$$-th columns, inclusive.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 100\,000$$$) — the number of strings. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq s_i \leq 10^{18}$$$) — the tuning of the ukulele. The third line contains an integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \leq q \leq 100\,000$$$) — the number of questions. The $$$k$$$-th among the following $$$q$$$ lines contains two integers $$$l_k$$$，$$$r_k$$$ ($$$0 \leq l_k \leq r_k \leq 10^{18}$$$) — a question from the fleas.
output_specification: Output one number for each question, separated by spaces — the number of different pitches.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1119D — Frets On Fire [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
